(ii) For every linear subspace T ⊆ R^m and v ∈ R^m, |p_{T⊥} v| = dist(v, T), where p_{T⊥} is the orthogonal projection onto T⊥.
(iii) For linear subspaces P, T ⊆ R^m with dim P = dim T, trace(p_{T⊥} ∘ p_P) = (1/2)|p_P − p_T|^2, where |·|^2 = hsNormSq.

subproblems.title: Smooth step profile on ℝ: 1 on (−∞, 1/2], 0 on [1, ∞), values in [0, 1], 3-Lipschitz
subproblems.statement: There is a C^infinity function φ : R → R such that (i) 0 <= φ(t) <= 1 for every t; (ii) φ(t) = 1 for every t <= 1/2; (iii) φ(t) = 0 for every t >= 1; (iv) φ is 3-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= 3|s − t| for all s, t ∈ R.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∃ φ : ℝ → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) φ ∧ (∀ t, 0 ≤ φ t ∧ φ t ≤ 1) ∧ (∀ t, t ≤ 1 / 2 → φ t = 1) ∧ (∀ t, 1 ≤ t → φ t = 0) ∧ LipschitzWith 3 φ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. Step 1 of the parent proof (Lemma A, ted_lemma_a_tilt_height) fixes phi in C^infinity(R, [0, 1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2], phi = 0 on [1, infinity) and |phi'| <= 3; this child supplies such a phi, with the derivative bound in the equivalent Lipschitz form LipschitzWith 3 phi, which the sibling radial_gradient consumes with K = 3. The parent uses the C^infinity property together with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2] to prove, as a local step, that zeta(x) = phi(|x - z|/r) is C^infinity, and the value properties to get 0 <= zeta <= 1, zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z) and zeta = 0 where |x - z| >= r. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.smooth_cutoff-a1.step_profile-a1 (candidate commit a848bdd), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; this proof is the argument formalized there. In Lean, ContDiff R (⊤ : ℕ∞) phi means C^infinity and LipschitzWith 3 phi (3 : NNReal) means |phi(s) - phi(t)| <= 3|s - t|.

Let S := Real.smoothTransition. Mathlib (Analysis/SpecialFunctions/SmoothTransition.lean) gives: S is C^infinity (Real.smoothTransition.contDiff); 0 <= S <= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.nonneg, Real.smoothTransition.le_one); S(s) = 0 for s <= 0 (Real.smoothTransition.zero_of_nonpos); S(s) = 1 for s >= 1 (Real.smoothTransition.one_of_one_le).

1. The bump g(t) := S(12(t - 1/2)) * S(12(1 - t)).
 (a) g is C^infinity: S is composed with the affine maps t -> 12(t - 1/2) and t -> 12(1 - t), and the two factors are multiplied. In particular g is continuous, hence interval-integrable on every interval.
 (b) 0 <= g(t) <= 1 for every t, as a product of two numbers in [0, 1].
 (c) If t <= 1/2 then 12(t - 1/2) <= 0, so the first factor vanishes and g(t) = 0. If t >= 1 then 12(1 - t) <= 0, so the second factor vanishes and g(t) = 0.
 (d) If 7/12 <= t <= 11/12 then 12(t - 1/2) >= 1 and 12(1 - t) >= 1, so both factors equal 1 and g(t) = 1.
2. The constant c := integral_{1/2}^{1} g(s) ds. By 1(d), integral_{7/12}^{11/12} g = integral_{7/12}^{11/12} 1 ds = 1/3. Since 1/2 <= 7/12 <= 11/12 <= 1, g >= 0 and g is integrable on [1/2, 1], the integral over the subinterval is at most the integral over [1/2, 1] (intervalIntegral.integral_mono_interval), so c >= 1/3. Hence c > 0 and c^{-1} <= 3.
3. The primitive F(t) := integral_{1/2}^{t} g(s) ds. Since g is continuous, the fundamental theorem of calculus (Continuous.integral_hasStrictDerivAt) shows that F has derivative g(t) at every t. So F is differentiable and deriv F = g, which is C^infinity by 1(a); hence F is C^infinity (contDiff_infty_iff_deriv).
4. Values of F.
 (a) If t <= 1/2, every s between t and 1/2 has s <= 1/2, so g(s) = 0 by 1(c) and F(t) = 0.
 (b) If t >= 1, additivity over adjacent intervals gives F(t) = integral_{1/2}^{1} g + integral_{1}^{t} g = c + 0 = c, because g = 0 on [1, t] by 1(c).
 (c) If 1/2 <= t <= 1, then 0 <= F(t) (g >= 0, intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg) and F(t) <= integral_{1/2}^{1} g = c (g >= 0 and [1/2, t] is contained in [1/2, 1]).
 Hence 0 <= F(t) <= c for every real t.
5. The profile phi(t) := 1 - c^{-1} F(t).
 (a) phi is C^infinity, as a constant minus a constant multiple of the C^infinity function F.
 (b) 0 <= phi(t) <= 1 for every t: by step 4 and c^{-1} > 0, 0 <= c^{-1} F(t) <= c^{-1} c = 1.
 (c) phi(t) = 1 - 0 = 1 for t <= 1/2, by 4(a).
 (d) phi(t) = 1 - c^{-1} c = 0 for t >= 1, by 4(b) and c != 0.
 (e) phi has derivative -c^{-1} g(t) at every t (step 3), and |-c^{-1} g(t)| = c^{-1} g(t) <= c^{-1} <= 3 by 1(b) and step 2. A differentiable function R -> R whose derivative has absolute value at most 3 everywhere is 3-Lipschitz by the mean value inequality (lipschitzWith_of_nnnorm_deriv_le); so LipschitzWith 3 phi.
6. By 5(a)-(e), phi satisfies all five required properties. QED
proof_key_steps: Bump g(t) = S(12(t - 1/2)) S(12(1 - t)), S = Real.smoothTransition: C^infinity, 0 <= g <= 1, g = 0 off (1/2, 1), g = 1 on [7/12, 11/12].
F(t) = integral_{1/2}^{t} g is C^infinity by the FTC, with F = 0 for t <= 1/2, F = c for t >= 1, 0 <= F <= c.
phi = 1 - c^{-1} F: C^infinity, values in [0, 1], 1 on (-inf, 1/2], 0 on [1, inf).

subproblems.title: The radial lift of a K-Lipschitz profile has ‖Dζ(x)‖ ≤ K/ρ everywhere
subproblems.statement: Let m ∈ N, ξ ∈ R^m (Euclidean space EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m)), ρ > 0, K ∈ ℝ≥0, and let φ : R → R be K-Lipschitz, i.e. |φ(s) − φ(t)| <= K|s − t| for all s, t. Put ζ(y) := φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ). Then for every x ∈ R^m the Fréchet derivative of ζ at x satisfies ‖Dζ(x)‖ <= K/ρ (operator norm). In Lean this is fderiv ℝ ζ x, which is 0 wherever ζ is not differentiable.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ξ : Rn m) (ρ : ℝ) (K : ℝ≥0) (φ : ℝ → ℝ), 0 < ρ → LipschitzWith K φ → ∀ x : Rn m, ‖fderiv ℝ (fun y : Rn m => φ (‖y - ξ‖ / ρ)) x‖ ≤ (K : ℝ) / ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Context. Step 1 of the parent proof (Lemma A, ted_lemma_a_tilt_height) needs |grad zeta| <= 3/r for the cutoff zeta(x) = phi(|x - z|/r); this is the case m = n + l, xi = z, rho = r, K = 3 of this child, applied to the 3-Lipschitz profile phi of the sibling step_profile (Amb n l is by definition Rn (n + l)). The parent uses the bound in steps 4 and 6 to control the cross term 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x'. It is the comparator-accepted declaration of DAG node root.tilt_excess_height_estimate-a1.smooth_cutoff-a1.radial_gradient_bound-a1 (candidate commit af64403), reused with its identical frozen Lean type; this proof is the argument formalized there.

Let m in N, xi in R^m = Rn m, rho > 0, K in NNReal, and let phi : R -> R be K-Lipschitz. Put zeta(y) := phi(||y - xi|| / rho).
1. Lipschitz estimate. For all y, w in R^m, since phi is K-Lipschitz and rho > 0,
 |zeta(y) - zeta(w)| <= K | ||y - xi||/rho - ||w - xi||/rho | = (K/rho) | ||y - xi|| - ||w - xi|| |,
 and by the reverse triangle inequality (abs_norm_sub_norm_le) | ||y - xi|| - ||w - xi|| | <= ||(y - xi) - (w - xi)|| = ||y - w||. Hence |zeta(y) - zeta(w)| <= (K/rho) dist(y, w).
2. So zeta is Lipschitz on R^m with the nonnegative constant K/rho. In Lean this is LipschitzWith (K / rho.toNNReal) zeta (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with step 1); the real value of the NNReal constant K / rho.toNNReal is (K : R)/rho, by NNReal.coe_div and Real.coe_toNNReal (rho >= 0).
3. If a function on a normed space is C-Lipschitz, its Frechet derivative has operator norm at most C at every point (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz); at points where the function is not differentiable, fderiv is 0 and the bound is trivial. Applying this with C = K / rho.toNNReal at x and rewriting C as (K : R)/rho by step 2 gives ||fderiv R zeta x|| <= K/rho for every x in R^m. QED
proof_key_steps: |zeta(y) - zeta(w)| <= (K/rho) | ||y - xi|| - ||w - xi|| | <= (K/rho) ||y - w|| (Lipschitz phi, rho > 0, reverse triangle inequality).
zeta is LipschitzWith (K / rho.toNNReal), whose real value is K/rho.
norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz gives ||fderiv R zeta x|| <= K/rho at every x.
